metadata.title: Decoding by Linear Programming
metadata.note: Worked-example gold annotation, NOT part of the 10-paper Benchmark-1 evaluation set. Iteratively curated from silver Opus scaffold; differences against silver report as the silver-vs-gold agreement metric.

nodes.name: Linear code decoding problem
nodes.statement: Recover input vector $f \in \R^n$ from corrupted measurements $y = Af + e$, where $A$ is an $m \times n$ coding matrix and $e$ is an arbitrary unknown vector of errors with $\|e\|_{\ell_0} \leq \rho \cdot m$.
nodes.statement_clean: Recover f from corrupted linear measurements y = Af + e where e is sparse.

nodes.name: Sparsity assumption on errors
nodes.statement: $\|e\|_{\ell_0} := |\{i : e_i \neq 0\}| \le \rho \cdot m$.
nodes.statement_clean: Errors are at most a rho-fraction of the output.

nodes.name: Annihilator reduction
nodes.statement: If $FA = 0$, then $\tilde y = F(Af + e) = Fe$, reducing decoding to recovering sparse $e$ from $Fe$.
nodes.statement_clean: Apply annihilator F (FA=0) to reduce decoding to sparse recovery.

nodes.name: $\ell_0$-minimization $(P_0)$
nodes.statement: $(P_0): \min_{d \in \R^m} \|d\|_{\ell_0}$ subject to $Fd = \tilde y$. Finding the sparsest solution to $Fd = \tilde y$.
nodes.statement_clean: Combinatorial sparsest-solution problem; NP-hard.

nodes.name: Basis Pursuit $(P_1)$
nodes.statement: $(P_1): \min_{d \in \R^m} \|d\|_{\ell_1}$ subject to $Fd = \tilde y$. Convex $\ell_1$ relaxation of $(P_0)$, recastable as a linear program.
nodes.statement_clean: Convex l1-minimization problem; the LP relaxation of P0.

nodes.name: Direct decoding LP $(P'_1)$
nodes.statement: $(P'_1): \min_{g \in \R^n} \|y - Ag\|_{\ell_1}$. Equivalent to $(P_1)$; recovers $f$ directly without forming the annihilator $F$.
nodes.statement_clean: Direct l1-minimization on the residual y-Ag, equivalent to basis pursuit.

nodes.name: LP form of $(P'_1)$
nodes.statement: $\min 1^T t$ subject to $-t \le y - Ag \le t$, with variables $t \in \R^m$ and $g \in \R^n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard LP reformulation of l1-minimization with slack variables t.

nodes.name: Restricted isometry constants
nodes.statement: For integer $1 \le S \le |J|$, $\delta_S$ is the smallest quantity such that $(1-\delta_S)\|c\|^2 \le \|F_T c\|^2 \le (1+\delta_S)\|c\|^2$ for all $T \subset J$ with $|T| \le S$ and all real coefficients $(c_j)_{j \in T}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Smallest delta_S making F_T act like a near-isometry on all S-sparse subsets.

nodes.name: Restricted orthogonality constants
nodes.statement: For $S+S' \le |J|$, $\theta_{S,S'}$ is the smallest quantity such that $|\langle F_T c, F_{T'} c' \rangle| \le \theta_{S,S'} \cdot \|c\|\,\|c'\|$ for all disjoint $T, T' \subseteq J$ with $|T| \le S$, $|T'| \le S'$.
nodes.statement_clean: Smallest theta_{S,S'} bounding inner products between disjoint S- and S'-sparse images of F.

nodes.name: $\delta_1$ unit-norm characterization
nodes.statement: $1 - \delta_1 \le \|v_j\|_H^2 \le 1 + \delta_1$ for all $j \in J$; in particular $\delta_1 = 0$ iff all $v_j$ have unit length.
nodes.statement_clean: delta_1 measures column-norm deviation from unit length.

nodes.name: Theta-delta comparison
nodes.statement: $\theta_{S,S'} \le \delta_{S+S'} \le \theta_{S,S'} + \max(\delta_S, \delta_{S'})$ for all $S, S'$.
nodes.statement_clean: Restricted-orthogonality and restricted-isometry constants are quantitatively comparable.

nodes.name: Unique sparse recovery from $\delta_{2S}<1$
nodes.statement: Suppose $S \ge 1$ with $\delta_{2S} < 1$ and $T \subset J$ with $|T| \le S$. Let $f := F_T c$. Then $T$ and the coefficients $(c_j)_{j \in T}$ can be uniquely reconstructed from $f$ and the $v_j$'s.
nodes.statement_clean: delta_{2S}<1 guarantees uniqueness of sparse representations (existence-only; brute force).
conclusions: $T$ and $(c_j)_{j \in T}$ are uniquely reconstructible from $f$ and the $v_j$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (unique sparse recovery)
nodes.statement: By contradiction: two distinct sparse representations would give $F_{T \cup T'} d = 0$ with $|T \cup T'| \le 2S$; $\delta_{2S} < 1$ via \eqref{frame} forces $\|d\|^2 = 0$, contradicting distinctness.

nodes.name: Main recovery theorem (Theorem 1.3)
nodes.statement: Suppose $S \ge 1$ with $\delta_S + \theta_S + \theta_{S,2S} < 1$, and $c$ is a real vector supported on $T \subset J$ with $|T| \le S$. Set $f := Fc$. Then $c$ is the unique minimizer of $(P_1): \min \|d\|_{\ell_1}$ subject to $Fd = f$.
nodes.statement_clean: Under the RIP+ROP condition, l1-minimization exactly recovers any S-sparse vector.
conclusions: $c$ is the unique minimizer of $(P_1)$ with $Fd = f$

nodes.name: Decoding theorem (Theorem 1.4)
nodes.statement: Suppose $F$ satisfies $FA = 0$ and $S \ge 1$ obeys the hypothesis of Theorem 1.3. Set $y = Af + e$ with $e$ supported on a set of size $\le S$. Then $f$ is the unique minimizer of $(P'_1): \min_{g \in \R^n} \|y - Ag\|_{\ell_1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Under the RIP+ROP condition, the LP decoder (P'_1) exactly recovers f despite arbitrary S-sparse corruption.

nodes.name: Gaussian matrices satisfy main hypothesis (Theorem 1.5)
nodes.statement: Assume $p \le m$ and let $F$ be a $p \times m$ matrix with i.i.d. Gaussian entries of mean zero and variance $1/p$. Then the condition of Theorem 1.3 holds with overwhelming probability provided $r = S/m < r^*(p,m)$, with explicit numerical thresholds e.g. $r \le 3.6 \cdot 10^{-4}$ at $p/m = 3/4$.
nodes.statement_clean: Gaussian random F obeys the RIP+ROP main condition w.h.p. for r below explicit numerical thresholds.

nodes.name: Gaussian decoding corollary
nodes.statement: Suppose $A$ is an $n \times m$ Gaussian matrix and set $p = m - n$. Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.5, the solution to $(P'_1)$ is unique and equal to $f$.
nodes.statement_clean: For Gaussian coding matrices A, LP decoding (P'_1) recovers f exactly.
conclusions: The solution to $(P'_1)$ is unique and equal to $f$

nodes.name: Dual sparse reconstruction property, $\ell_2$ version (Lemma 2.1)
nodes.statement: Let $S, S' \ge 1$ with $\delta_S < 1$ and $c$ supported on $T \subset J$ with $|T| \le S$. Then $\exists w \in H$ with $\langle w, v_j \rangle_H = c_j$ for $j \in T$, an exceptional set $E$ disjoint from $T$ with $|E| \le S'$, and $|\langle w, v_j \rangle| \le \frac{\theta_{S,S'}}{(1-\delta_S)\sqrt{S'}}\|c\|$ for $j \notin T \cup E$.
nodes.statement_clean: Constructs a dual certificate w with l2 control of inner products outside T (with a small exceptional set).
conclusions: $\exists\, w \in H$ with $\langle w, v_j\rangle_H = c_j$ for $j \in T$
$\exists$ exceptional set $E$ disjoint from $T$ with $|E| \le S'$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Construct $w := F_T (F_T^* F_T)^{-1} c_T$ via invertibility of $F_T^* F_T$ from $\delta_S < 1$; bound $\|F_{T'}^* w\|_{\ell_2}$ via duality; define exceptional set $E$ where the bound is exceeded.

nodes.name: Dual sparse reconstruction property, $\ell_\infty$ version (Lemma 2.2)
nodes.statement: Let $S \ge 1$ with $\delta_S + \theta_{S,2S} < 1$ and $c$ supported on $T \subset J$ with $|T| \le S$. Then $\exists w \in H$ with $\langle w, v_j\rangle_H = c_j$ for $j \in T$, and $|\langle w, v_j \rangle| \le \frac{\theta_S}{(1 - \delta_S - \theta_{S,2S})\sqrt{S}}\|c\|$ for $j \notin T$.
nodes.statement_clean: Constructs a dual certificate w with l-infinity control of inner products outside T (no exceptional set).
conclusions: $\exists\, w \in H$ with $\langle w, v_j\rangle_H = c_j$ for $j \in T$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.2 (iterative construction)
nodes.statement: Iterate Lemma 2.1: build $w_n$ correcting the previous step's exceptional set $T_{n-1}$, then set $w := \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} (-1)^{n-1} w_n$; absolute convergence and term-cancellation on $T_n$ give the $\ell_\infty$ bound via geometric series.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.3
nodes.statement: By duality: take $w$ from Lemma 2.2 satisfying (i) $\langle w, v_j\rangle = \sgn(c_j)$ on $T$ and (ii) $|\langle w, v_j\rangle| < 1$ off $T$. Comparing $\|d\|_{\ell_1}$ with $\|c\|_{\ell_1}$ via $w$ forces $d_j = 0$ off $T$, then $\delta_S < 1$ gives $d = c$.

nodes.name: Possible improvement of the $\delta_S + \theta_{S,S} + \theta_{S,2S} < 1$ condition
nodes.statement: The condition $\delta_S + \theta_{S,S} + \theta_{S,2S} < 1$ might be pushed further by replacing annihilation in the iteration with mere moderation of $w_{n-1}$; not pursued here due to complications.
nodes.statement_clean: Hypothesis could be sharpened by softer iterative correction; left to future work.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (theta-delta)
nodes.statement: First $\theta_{S,S'} \le \delta_{S+S'}$ via the parallelogram identity applied to disjoint unit-norm sums. Second $\delta_{S+S'} \le \max(\delta_S, \delta_{S'}) + \theta_S$ via a partition of $\tilde T$ into $T \cup T'$ and \eqref{frame}+\eqref{ortho}.

nodes.name: Marchenko-Pastur a.s. limits for $F_T^* F_T$
nodes.statement: $\lambda_{\min}(F_T^* F_T) \to (1-\sqrt{\gamma})^2$ a.s. and $\lambda_{\max}(F_T^* F_T) \to (1+\sqrt{\gamma})^2$ a.s. as $p, |T| \to \infty$ with $|T|/p \to \gamma \le 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Marchenko-Pastur limits for extremal eigenvalues of Wishart matrices.

nodes.name: Ledoux Gaussian concentration for singular values (cited)
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{P}(\sigma_{\max}(F_T) > 1 + \sqrt{|T|/p} + o(1) + t) \le e^{-pt^2/2}$ and $\mathbb{P}(\sigma_{\min}(F_T) < 1 - \sqrt{|T|/p} + o(1) - t) \le e^{-pt^2/2}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Gaussian concentration gives sub-Gaussian deviation bounds for singular values of F_T.
assumptions: $F_T$ is the standard $|T| \times p$ Gaussian block

nodes.name: Uniform Gaussian RIP bound (Lemma 3.1)
nodes.statement: Let $r = S/m$, $f(r) := \sqrt{m/p} (\sqrt{r} + \sqrt{2H(r)})$ where $H(q) = -q\log q - (1-q)\log(1-q)$. For each $\epsilon > 0$, the restricted isometry constant of a $p \times m$ Gaussian matrix obeys $\mathbb{P}(1 + \delta_S > [1 + (1+\epsilon) f(r)]^2) \le 2 e^{-mH(r)\epsilon/2}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Uniform large-deviation bound on delta_S for Gaussian matrices via union bound + entropy.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: Apply concentration bounds for fixed $T$, take a union bound over $\binom{m}{S}$ subsets using Stirling's $\log\binom{m}{S} = mH(r) + O(\log m)$, then choose $\eta_p + t = (1+\epsilon)\sqrt{m/p}\sqrt{2H(r)}$.

nodes.name: Sufficient condition for main hypothesis under Gaussian model
nodes.statement: $\delta_S + \delta_{2S} + \delta_{3S} < \rho_{p/m}(r)$ where $\rho_{p/m}(r) = \sum_{j=1}^{3} -1 + [1 + f(jr)]^2$, with very high probability.
nodes.statement_clean: Combines Lemma 3.1 across S, 2S, 3S to bound the main-hypothesis sum.

nodes.name: Numerical experiments for $(P'_1)$ recovery
nodes.statement: Empirical study of $(P'_1)$ on Gaussian $A$: for $m = 2n$ ($m \in \{512, 1024\}$) recovery succeeds whenever the corrupted fraction is $\le 17\%$; for $m = 4n$ ($m = 512$) recovery succeeds whenever the corrupted fraction is $\le 34\%$.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical breakpoints: ~17% corruption tolerated for m=2n, ~34% for m=4n.

nodes.name: Optimal recovery of compressible signals (Theorem 5.1)
nodes.statement: Let $F$ be the measurement matrix in $y = F\alpha$. Let $S \le K$ with $\delta_S + 2\theta_S + \theta_{S,2S} < 1$ and $\lambda = K/S$. Then the solution $\alpha^\sharp$ to $\min \|\tilde\alpha\|_{\ell_1}$ s.t. $F\tilde\alpha = y$ obeys $\sup_{\alpha \in \cF_s(B)} \|\alpha - \alpha^\sharp\| \le C \cdot (K/\lambda)^{-(s-1/2)}$.
nodes.statement_clean: L1-minimization gives near-optimal reconstruction of compressible (power-law) signals.

nodes.name: Compressible signal class $\cF_s(B)$
nodes.statement: $\cF_s(B)$ is the class of $\alpha \in \R^m$ whose entries, rearranged in decreasing order of magnitude $|\alpha|_{(1)} \ge |\alpha|_{(2)} \ge \cdots$, obey $|\alpha|_{(k)} \le B \cdot k^{-s}$ for some $s \ge 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Class of signals with power-law decay of sorted magnitudes.

nodes.name: Uniform Uncertainty Principle (UUP)
nodes.statement: A random matrix $F$ obeys the UUP with oversampling factor $\lambda$ if $\delta_S \le 1/2$ for $S = \rho \cdot K/\lambda$, with probability at least $1 - O(N^{-\gamma/\rho})$ for some fixed $\gamma > 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Probabilistic RIP-type condition with controlled tail.

nodes.name: Exact Reconstruction Principle (ERP)
nodes.statement: $F$ obeys the ERP with oversampling factor $\lambda$ if for each fixed $T$ with $|T| \le S$ and each sign vector $c$ on $T$, with overwhelming probability there exists $w \in H$ with $\langle w, v_j \rangle = c_j$ on $T$ and $|\langle w, v_j\rangle| \le 1/2$ off $T$.
nodes.statement_clean: Existence of dual certificate w for each sign pattern, with high probability.

nodes.name: ERP is redundant given main hypothesis
nodes.statement: Theorem 5.1 shows the ERP is redundant: if $F$ obeys the main hypothesis it satisfies both UUP and ERP (the latter via Lemma 2.2). The ability to recover compressible signals reduces purely to the UUP.
nodes.statement_clean: ERP can be derived from the RIP+ROP main hypothesis, so only UUP is needed.

nodes.name: Tight cut-off and finite-alphabet extensions
nodes.statement: Improve Theorem 1.5 beyond the ~2% cut-off (current approach hits $\liminf \delta_S + \theta_{S,S} + \theta_{S,2S} \ge J(m/p \cdot r)$ where $J(r) = 2\sqrt{r} + r + (2+\sqrt{2})\sqrt{r(1-r)} + \sqrt{r(1-2r)}$); also extend the LP-decoding analysis to inputs from finite alphabets.
nodes.statement_clean: Improve the recovery threshold beyond ~2% and handle finite-alphabet codes.

nodes.name: LP decoder for $(P'_1)$
nodes.statement: Solve the linear program $\min 1^T t$ s.t. $-t \le y - Ag \le t$ to recover $f$ from corrupted measurements $y = Af + e$.
output: Recovered signal $g^* = f$ (under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.4)

nodes.name: Set up contradiction with two distinct sparse representations
nodes.statement: Suppose for contradiction that $f$ has two distinct sparse representations $f = F_T c = F_{T'} c'$ with $|T|, |T'| \le S$. Then $F_{T \cup T'} d = 0$ for $d_j := c_j 1_{j \in T} - c'_{j} 1_{j \in T'}$.

nodes.name: Apply restricted isometry to derive contradiction
nodes.statement: Take norms of $F_{T \cup T'} d = 0$ and apply \eqref{frame} with $|T \cup T'| \le 2S$ and the hypothesis $\delta_{2S} < 1$ to conclude $\|d\|^2 = 0$, contradicting distinctness of the two representations.

nodes.name: Set up adjoint and bound spectrum of $F_T^* F_T$
nodes.statement: Define $F_T : \ell_2(T) \to H$, $F_T c_T := \sum_{j \in T} c_j v_j$ and adjoint $F_T^* w := (\langle w, v_j\rangle)_{j \in T}$. By \eqref{frame}, $1 - \delta_S \le \lambda_{\min}(F_T^* F_T) \le \lambda_{\max}(F_T^* F_T) \le 1 + \delta_S$, so $F_T^* F_T$ is invertible with $\|(F_T^* F_T)^{-1}\| \le 1/(1-\delta_S)$.

nodes.name: Define dual certificate $w$
nodes.statement: Set $w := F_T (F_T^* F_T)^{-1} c_T$. Then $F_T^* w = c_T$, i.e. $\langle w, v_j \rangle_H = c_j$ for all $j \in T$, and $\|w\| \le K \|c_T\|$ with $K = \sqrt{1+\delta_S}/(1-\delta_S)$.

nodes.name: Bound $\|F_{T'}^* w\|_{\ell_2}$ on disjoint sets via duality
nodes.statement: For any $T' \subseteq J \setminus T$ with $|T'| \le S'$ and any $d_{T'}$, expand $\langle F_{T'}^* w, d_{T'} \rangle$ and apply \eqref{ortho} with restricted-orthogonality constant $\theta_{S,S'}$ together with $\|(F_T^* F_T)^{-1}\| \le 1/(1-\delta_S)$ to obtain $\|F_{T'}^* w\|_{\ell_2(T')} \le \frac{\theta_{S,S'}}{1-\delta_S}\|c_T\|$.

nodes.name: Define exceptional set $E$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Let $E := \{j \in J \setminus T : |\langle w, v_j\rangle| > \frac{\theta_{S,S'}}{(1-\delta_S)\sqrt{S'}}\|c_T\|\}$. The $\ell_2$ bound forces $|E| \le S'$ (else a subset $T' \subseteq E$ of size $S'$ contradicts the bound). The lemma's claims follow.

nodes.name: Base step: apply Lemma 2.1 to obtain $w_1, T_1$
nodes.statement: Normalize $\sum_{j \in T} |c_j|^2 = \sqrt{S}$ and set $T_0 := T$. Apply Lemma 2.1 to obtain $w_1 \in H$ and exceptional set $T_1$ disjoint from $T_0$ with $|T_1| \le S$, $\langle w_1, v_j\rangle = c_j$ for $j \in T_0$, $\ell_2$-control of $w_1$ on $T_1$, and $\ell_\infty$ bound off $T_0 \cup T_1$.

nodes.name: Iterative step: build $w_{n+1}$ to cancel $w_n$ on $T_n$
nodes.statement: For each $n \ge 1$ apply Lemma 2.1 again to construct $w_{n+1} \in H$ and $T_{n+1}$ with $T_n \cap (T_0 \cup T_{n+1}) = \emptyset$, $\langle w_{n+1}, v_j\rangle = \langle w_n, v_j\rangle$ for $j \in T_n$, $\langle w_{n+1}, v_j\rangle = 0$ for $j \in T_0$, and decaying $\ell_\infty$ and $\ell_2$ bounds with factor $(\theta_{S,2S}/(1-\delta_S))^n$.

nodes.name: Define telescoping sum $w := \sum_n (-1)^{n-1} w_n$
nodes.statement: Since $\theta_{S,2S}/(1-\delta_S) < 1$ by hypothesis, the series $w := \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} (-1)^{n-1} w_n$ is absolutely convergent and well-defined in $H$.

nodes.name: Verify $\langle w, v_j \rangle = c_j$ on $T_0$
nodes.statement: For $j \in T_0$: $\langle w_1, v_j\rangle = c_j$ and $\langle w_n, v_j\rangle = 0$ for $n \ge 2$, hence $\langle w, v_j\rangle = c_j$ for all $j \in T_0$.

nodes.name: Bound $|\langle w, v_j \rangle|$ off $T_0$ via term cancellation and geometric series
nodes.statement: For $j \notin T_0$ define $I_j = \{n \ge 1 : j \in T_n\}$. Since $T_n, T_{n+1}$ are disjoint, the integers in $I_j$ are spaced $\ge 2$ apart, so consecutive terms in $\sum_n (-1)^{n-1}\langle w_n, v_j\rangle$ cancel on $I_j$. The remaining terms are bounded by $\frac{\theta_{S,S}}{1-\delta_S}(\theta_{S,2S}/(1-\delta_S))^{n-1}$; geometric summation yields $|\langle w, v_j\rangle| \le \frac{\theta_{S,S}}{1-\delta_S - \theta_{S,2S}}$, giving the claimed $\ell_\infty$ bound after rescaling.

nodes.name: Existence of minimizer and lower bound on $\|d\|_{\ell_1}$
nodes.statement: Standard convex arguments give existence of a minimizer $d$ to $(P_1)$. Since $c$ is feasible, $\|d\|_{\ell_1} \le \|c\|_{\ell_1} = \sum_{j \in T} |c_j|$.

nodes.name: Take dual certificate $w$ from Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 2.2 to obtain $w$ with (i) $\langle w, v_j\rangle = \sgn(c_j)$ for $j \in T$ and (ii) $|\langle w, v_j\rangle| < 1$ for $j \notin T$ (the latter holds under $\delta_S + \theta_{S,S} + \theta_{S,2S} < 1$).

nodes.name: Compute lower bound on $\|d\|_{\ell_1}$ via $w$
nodes.statement: Decompose $\|d\|_{\ell_1} = \sum_{j \in T} |c_j + (d_j - c_j)| + \sum_{j \notin T} |d_j|$, then use $\sgn(c_j)$ on $T$ and $\langle w, v_j\rangle$ off $T$ to show $\|d\|_{\ell_1} \ge \sum_{j \in T} |c_j| + \langle w, \sum_j d_j v_j - \sum_{j \in T} c_j v_j\rangle = \sum_{j \in T} |c_j|$ (using $\sum_j d_j v_j = f = \sum_{j \in T} c_j v_j$).

nodes.name: Force $d_j = 0$ off $T$ and conclude $d = c$
nodes.statement: All inequalities are equalities; since $|\langle w, v_j\rangle| < 1$ off $T$, this forces $d_j = 0$ for $j \notin T$. Then $\sum_{j \in T} (d_j - c_j) v_j = 0$, and \eqref{frame} with $\delta_S < 1$ gives $d_j = c_j$ on $T$. Hence $d = c$.

nodes.name: First inequality $\theta_{S,S'} \le \delta_{S+S'}$ via parallelogram identity
nodes.statement: By homogeneity, suffices to bound $|\langle \sum_T c_j v_j, \sum_{T'} c'_{j'} v_{j'}\rangle| \le \delta_{S+S'}$ for disjoint $T, T'$ with unit-norm coefficients. Apply \eqref{frame} to the sum and difference $\sum_T c_j v_j \pm \sum_{T'} c'_{j'} v_{j'}$ (each supported on $\le S+S'$ indices) and the parallelogram identity $\langle f, g\rangle = (\|f+g\|^2 - \|f-g\|^2)/4$.

nodes.name: Second inequality $\delta_{S+S'} \le \max(\delta_S, \delta_{S'}) + \theta_S$ via partition
nodes.statement: By homogeneity, bound $|\langle \sum_{\tilde T} c_j v_j, \sum_{\tilde T} c_{j'} v_{j'}\rangle - 1|$ for $|\tilde T| \le S + S'$ with $\sum |c_j|^2 = 1$. Partition $\tilde T = T \cup T'$ ($|T| \le S$, $|T'| \le S'$) with $\sum_T |c_j|^2 = \alpha$. Apply \eqref{frame} on $T$ and $T'$ separately and \eqref{ortho} on the cross term to obtain $|\cdots - 1| \le \delta_S \alpha + \delta_{S'}(1-\alpha) + 2\theta_S \sqrt{\alpha(1-\alpha)} \le \max(\delta_S, \delta_{S'}) + \theta_S$.

nodes.name: Reduce to $|T| = S$ via monotonicity of eigenvalues under inclusion
nodes.statement: Since $T' \subset T$ implies $\lambda_{\min}(F_T^* F_T) \le \lambda_{\min}(F_{T'}^* F_{T'}) \le \lambda_{\max}(F_{T'}^* F_{T'}) \le \lambda_{\max}(F_T^* F_T)$, attention may be restricted to subsets $T$ of size exactly $S$.

nodes.name: Union bound over $\binom{m}{S}$ subsets using Ledoux concentration
nodes.statement: Apply \eqref{eq:concentration} for each fixed $|T| = S$ and union-bound: $\mathbb{P}(\sup_{|T|=S} \lambda_{\max} > (1 + \sqrt{S/p} + \eta_p + t)^2) \le \binom{m}{S} e^{-pt^2/2}$.

nodes.name: Stirling estimate for $\log\binom{m}{S}$
nodes.statement: From Stirling $\log m! = m\log m - m + O(\log m)$, $\log \binom{m}{S} = m H(r) + O(\log m)$ where $r = S/m$ and $H$ is the binary entropy. Thus the union bound becomes $e^{m H(r)} \cdot e^{O(\log m)} \cdot e^{-pt^2/2}$.

nodes.name: Choose $t$ to balance entropy term and conclude
nodes.statement: Fix $\eta_p + t = (1+\epsilon) \sqrt{m/p}\sqrt{2H(r)}$ with $\eta_p \le (\epsilon/2)\sqrt{m/p}\sqrt{2H(r)}$ for large $m,p$. Then $\mathbb{P}(\sup_T \lambda_{\max} > (1 + \sqrt{S/p} + \epsilon\sqrt{m/p}\sqrt{2H(r)})^2) \le e^{-mH(r)\epsilon/2}$. The same bound holds for $\lambda_{\min}$; the lemma follows.
